title: VaultTec — Phase 5 Trend-Following & Stress Test Report
method: Two paper-only tests on delayed real yfinance history, 12 symbols, walk-forward, signals from history up to the trade day only — no look-ahead. Every trade goes through the real PaperTradingEngine and Risk Engine, balanced profile, $10,000 virtual cash, long-only, 10-day exit. Every variant keeps a stop-loss; the stop is never removed. (a) Trend-following: SMA crossover (SMA-10 cross above SMA-30) and MACD crossover (MACD cross above signal line), exactly as defined in analytics/backtest.py, with wide-6 exits (6% stop / 9% target, 1.5:1), on OOS-1/2/3, the Phase 4 window (re-run, in-sample), and FRESH-1/2/3. Trend entries are checked on EVERY bar because a crossover is a single-bar event a 5-day step would miss; mean-reversion entries in Phases 4b–4d used a 5-day step because their triggers are persistent states. (b) Stress: RSI + Bollinger mean-reversion under baseline (3% / 4.5%), wide-5 (5% / 7.5%) and wide-6 (6% / 9%) on one more fresh window, FRESH-4 (2022-09-12 → 2023-03-10), with the Phase 4d method (70 days warm-up, 5-day steps). Fetched histories are cached to data/fresh-cache/ as they arrive; FRESH-1/2/3 histories were already cached from Phase 4d and were not re-fetched.

note: Nothing here proves future profits: past performance does not guarantee future results. Trend trade counts are not directly comparable with mean-reversion trade counts because trend entries are checked every bar while mean-reversion entries were checked every 5 days — P&L, win rate, and expectancy per trade are the comparison. The FRESH-4 stress check is a single window, so a hold-up there is weaker evidence than the Phase 4d three-window hold-up. Related work: a parallel Phase 4e run (validation/phase4e-trend-following-report.md) tested a different trend entry — buy when close > SMA-20 > SMA-50, a persistent state, on 5-day steps — on FRESH-1/2/3 only, from cache: wide-6 422 trades, 61.8% win, +$5,163.64 pooled fresh. It did not cover OOS-2, so it cannot answer the falling-window question; this Phase 5 test uses crossover entries (SMA-10/30, MACD) on the OOS + fresh windows instead. The two trend definitions are not the same strategy and their trade counts are not comparable. Live paper trades over real days plus a compliance/legal review are still required before any real money is considered.
